description_full: DeNA Co., Ltd. develops and operates various mobile and online services in Japan and internationally. It operates DeNA games, a free-to-play mobile apps and browser games; Mobage, an entertainment platform; Yahoo! Mobage, which offers social games for PC browsers; AndApp, a platform that allows users to play mobile game apps on PC browsers under the same user account; Pococha, a social live streaming community; and IRIAM, an app where users can live stream as an anime characters. The company also operates kencom, which supports health insurance societies to manage their members' health data; and ONSEI, an AI-driven cognitive self-check app. In addition, it operates MENKYO, which enables cognitive function test for elderly drivers seeking license renewal; MOGI, a cognitive function test similar to MENKYO; SHINRI-ADAS, a cognitive functional test; Join, a communication app; MySOS, a life-saving and health support app with health and medical record for the user and their family; Team, a solution that connects medical and healthcare services and supports multi-professional collaboration; Join Mobile Clinic, an integrated telemedicine support solution that combines portable medical devices and Join; and Tsunaken, a health checkup online digital transformation solution. Further, the company operates DENA SPORTS GROUP, Yokohama DeNA Baystars, Kawasaki Brave Thunders, S.C.SAGAMIHARA, Virtual KEIBI System, DeNA AI, Strategic Investment Office, and Delight Ventures. DeNA Co., Ltd. was incorporated in 1999 and is headquartered in Shibuya, Japan.

financial_summary: Dena Co., Ltd. is a small-cap industrials business with a $1.5B market cap on $925M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -1% over the past three years — essentially flat, and a business treading water is rarely a path to compounding. Operating margins are expanding by +3.2pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 5% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 51% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $177M in free cash flow — roughly 19 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.02× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage runs at 5.0×.
Shareholder yield is only 0.9%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 47% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

news_headlines.title: DeNA (OTCMKTS:DNACF) Issues Quarterly Earnings Results, Misses Estimates By $0.09 EPS

sect: Its 13% operating margin is roughly in line with the Industrials median (9%).
Its share of sector profits slightly exceeds its share of revenue (1.14x).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.01 across 548 companies in the universe; the top four hold 9% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted lower, down 9% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has rebounded 6% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 14% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 34% and a beta of 0.46, it is more defensive than the market.
Trading is thin (about $3K a day), below the $1.0M liquidity floor flagged; building a position would move the price.
In past sell-offs it fell 38% in the 2020 crash and 18% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The stock trades 22% below its DCF fair value of $20.26, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 5%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $16.97 to $24.96 (P10-P90).
On multiples it looks cheap against Industrials peers: P/E 7.2 vs 24.1 and P/FCF 8.3 vs 22.9 (sector median).
Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 12.0% (above the risk-free rate).
The price implies 14.9% annual cash-flow growth, 6pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 5% falls short of the cost of capital of 7.2%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 10.44).
It runs a 51% gross margin and converts 19% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 8/9 and cash conversion of 2.02x.
ROE of 8% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.4x equity multiplier).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $552.2M.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 3.4, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at -0.6% over 3 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 4.5% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
own: Insiders own 46.9%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 25%.
Shareholder yield is a modest 0.9% (2.6% in dividends).
It has paid a dividend for 12 consecutive years.
people: With about 2,483 employees, each generates about $373K of revenue, in line with the Industrials median.
That works out to $71K of free cash flow per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
Compensation governance scores well (1/10, lower is better).
